question: What validation and enforcement contract should OpenClaw use for prompt-bearing Markdown across local runtime ingestion and ClawHub distribution?
rationale: Code cannot safely infer which patterns are forbidden, which are warnings, whether existing files remain compatible, how overrides work, or which enforcement belongs in OpenClaw versus ClawHub.

options.title: Shared findings, boundary-specific enforcement
options.body: Create one typed analyzer, warn by default for existing local content, allow only narrowly approved critical install blocks, and let ClawHub publish or tag findings under its own policy.

options.title: Audit-only scanner
options.body: Expose findings through security audit and ClawHub metadata without changing runtime ingestion or install behavior.

options.title: Mandatory rejection
options.body: Reject any prompt-bearing Markdown matching the selected rules at read, install, and publish boundaries, accepting compatibility and false-positive costs.

recommendation.title: Shared findings, boundary-specific enforcement
recommendation.body: Create one typed analyzer, warn by default for existing local content, allow only narrowly approved critical install blocks, and let ClawHub publish or tag findings under its own policy.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest cross-surface history and already framed the unresolved product and security boundary in the issue discussion.
